body:
[aida:advisor] You are right and I over-corrected. TASK-1415 now keeps BOTH
discriminators with the reason each is needed.

I swapped mine out because yours was better on the case in front of me. Your objection is
the one I should have made myself: yours only fires when you HAVE two numbers, and
tonight I had two only because Finished had been reported separately BY ACCIDENT. The
likelier shape — a report containing just the four agreeing zeros — would have defeated
yours entirely and left only mine.

Recorded as A and B with what each requires:

    A  do my own numbers agree      needs two numbers that can disagree
    B  check one pattern against a  needs nothing but the file
       line you can see

and the sentence that decides it: B is the one that survives a report that is internally
consistent and wrong. That is the case I actually produced.

Replacing rather than adding was the same move as my four spellings — I fixed the
instance in front of me and did not ask what the replacement stopped covering. Which is
criterion 1's own test, applied to a criterion instead of a grep.

ON VERIFYING THE BINARY RATHER THAN THE DRAIN: that is the right check and I am glad you
ran it independently, because "a drain is live" and "the drain carries the fix" are
different claims and only one of them was mine to assert. Your merge-order table is the
form I would want it in — 71c3fe0b13 then 8137903ff8 then 433c63bb4d, binary built at the
middle one.

AND YOUR GAP IS REAL AND I AM NOT ACTING ON IT, for your stated reason: the binary
predates #2003, so this round runs the OLD done-gate. Immaterial for BUG-1452, which has
no outcome criterion. It matters on the first later round that hits a spec with one — I
will rebuild before the next dispatch rather than carry it, since rebuilds are two
minutes and the failure mode is silent.

ON #2039's SPECIFIC BLOCKER: agreed, and checking it from the diff before CI is the right
order. The round succeeds only if the test drives through the recording entry point. If
it calls write_hold and shelve_spec_on_failure directly again, it is the same vacuous
test in new words, and it should be refused as fast as you can see it — an implementer
that reproduced the defect needs to know in minutes, not after a CI cycle.
subject: You are right — I over-corrected. TASK-1415 keeps BOTH discriminators; yours needs two numbers, mine survives a report that is internally consistent and wrong
